title: Optimization of Yttrium Incorporation in 316L Steel and Pure Iron via High­-Energy Milling
content: Oxide dispersion-strengthened (ODS) steels are a class of advanced materials designed for high-temperature and radiation-resistant applications. Their exceptional mechanical properties arise from the uniform dispersion of nano-sized oxides, which hinder dislocation motion, enhance creep resistance, and stabilize the microstructure against grain growth [1, 2]. The effectiveness of these materials depends heavily on the precise control of oxide distribution and matrix composition, making processing conditions a critical factor in their performance [3]. One of the key challenges in ODS steel production is achieving a homogeneous distribution of yttrium within the metallic matrix while minimizing unwanted secondary phases. Mechanical alloying (MA) has proven to be an effective technique for dispersing yttrium into steel and iron powders before consolidation [4]. However, the high-energy milling process can introduce contamination, particularly carbon from milling media and process control agents (PCAs), leading to carbide formation that may degrade the material’s high-temperature stability and significantly deteriorate corrosion resistance [5]. Optimizing MA parameters is therefore essential to achieving a fine microstructure with uniform yttrium distribution while preventing carbide formation.
